chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify "the brief that already holds the folded state does not fold the log again to say it" (its own docstring), but it only verifies the second half of that promise. The pre-patch assertion (`assert US.doctor_notes(old, _load(old, 'starter')[2])`) calls `US.doctor_notes` directly, not `lifecycle.brief`; and after monkeypatching, the only assertions are `folds == []`. So if the half of the change in `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py` is wrong — e.g. `_upgrade_notices` is handed a state that does not say the project is behind, or the note is filtered/dropped so the timeout note never appears in the brief output — every assertion still holds (`folds == []` is trivially satisfied whenever the brief does no folding), and the regression the parent roborev finding was about (the note must keep repeating in the brief until the project is upgraded) ships untested. Concretely: replace the brief's start-check note with `[]` (drop it) and this test still passes green, while `ddflow brief` silently stops warning about the unfinished check. The test should also assert the remedy text appears in the brief text for both calls.
